basics.name: Sobhan Asasi
basics.label: PhD Researcher, CVSSP, University of Surrey
basics.summary: PhD researcher at the Centre for Vision, Speech and Signal Processing (CVSSP), University of Surrey, supervised by Prof. Richard Bowden. My thesis is on sign language recognition and translation, with a focus on gloss-free translation, motion-level knowledge transfer across sign languages, and transferable sign representations. I work on vision-language models and multimodal LLMs for sign language translation. First author at ECCV 2026, BMVC 2025 and ACM IVA 2025, co-author of an evaluation study in CVIU, and first author of a further preprint under review. Keywords: vision-language models, multimodal LLMs, video understanding, sign language translation, contrastive representation learning, cross-lingual transfer.

work.name: Centre for Vision, Speech and Signal Processing (CVSSP), University of Surrey
work.summary: Research on gloss-free sign language translation with vision-language models and multimodal LLMs, under the supervision of Prof. Richard Bowden.
highlights: Own the full research stack for gloss-free sign language translation: data pipelines, pre-training of video-language models on large-scale datasets, multi-GPU training, and evaluation across multiple sign language corpora.
Devised a cross-language transfer method that lets a single model serve multiple sign languages, removing the per-language retraining that dataset-specific pipelines require.
Built a VideoLLM-based translation framework that generates fine-grained, temporally-aware descriptions of hand motion and contrastively aligns them with video features during pre-training.
Built a reproducible evaluation protocol that exposed systematic bias in previously reported gloss-free translation results, re-establishing a reliable baseline for the field.

work.name: Electronic Research Institute (ERI) at Sharif University of Technology
work.summary: Conducted research and development on machine learning and speech processing systems, focusing on dataset creation and model development for speech processing tasks.
highlights: Covered dataset creation, model development, and multi-GPU training on downstream speech datasets.

Built a speech enhancement front-end for an ASR pipeline, trained so enhanced-speech embeddings match their clean-speech targets under environmental noise and reverberation; exported to ONNX for low-resource inference.
Designed a frame-level voice activity detector (CNN/RNN/FNN) to cut ASR compute and error, reaching higher accuracy than contemporary models with fewer parameters and lower CPU runtime.

work.name: Sensifai
highlights: Evaluated and adapted a modular licence plate recognition pipeline (TensorFlow SSD detector served through OpenCV DNN, CRAFT character detection, contour-based segmentation), extending it to additional plate templates and benchmarking end-to-end recognition accuracy.

Assessed a Pytesseract-based OCR pipeline for structured document extraction, locating target keywords and their associated values across PDFs of differing layouts, and adapted the extraction logic to support a new document template.
